title: Steady Spine
intro: Two or three times a week, alongside your normal training. We walk first, then free up the hips and upper back, then build the brace that keeps the middle still, then unload. Nothing here stretches or rolls your lower back, because that is the one thing a sore back does not want.

before.label: Who it's for
before.text: Ordinary back pain that a doctor or physio has already looked at and cleared you to train through.

before.label: Stop and get it looked at
before.text: Pain running down a leg, numbness, weakness in a leg or foot, or numbness between your legs. Also if your back pain started after a fall or a hit, or if it wakes you at night. If your bladder or bowel control changes, get seen the same day.

before.label: While you train
before.text: A bit of ache is fine. Sharp pain isn't, and neither is pain that builds through a set or feels worse the next morning. If it builds, stop that exercise. If it's sharp, stop the session.

exercises.name: Easy Walk
exercises.note: An ache you can breathe through is fine, a sharp pain is not — stop that exercise and tell me.

good: Easy pace, tall through the spine, let the arms swing
Nothing should tighten up as you go
bad: Skipping it to get to the exercises

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.note: Wake the glutes up here and your back does less of their work for the rest of the session.

good: Push through your heels until your hips are level
Feel the glutes doing it, not your lower back
bad: Arching your back to lift higher

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Hip Flexor with Overhead Reach
exercises.note: We free the hips and upper back so your lower back stops doing their job.

good: Squeeze the back glute, then reach the same-side arm overhead
Feel it at the front of the back hip, never in your lower back
bad: Arching the lower back to feel more

good: Rotate both knees slowly to the other side, chest tall
Go only as far as you can control
bad: Forcing the knees down with your hands

good: Knees stacked and together, open the top arm and follow it with your eyes
Feel the turn in your ribs, not your lower back
Ankle across the opposite knee, pull the bottom thigh towards you
Feel it deep in the glute of the crossed leg
bad: Pulling hard enough that your hips lift off the floor

exercises.name: Modified Curl-Up
exercises.note: 10 sec hold. Leave this one for an hour after you wake up, when the discs are most swollen.

good: Hands under the small of your back, lift head and shoulders barely an inch
Your lower back keeps its arch the whole set
bad: Letting the back flatten into the floor — that is a sit-up

exercises.name: Side Bridge
exercises.note: 10 sec hold. Start on your knees and only move to the feet when the knee version is easy on both sides.

good: Elbow under the shoulder, lift the hips into a straight line
Hips stacked, nothing rolling forward

exercises.name: Bird Dog
exercises.note: 10 sec hold. Six reps, then four, then two, so it gets easier as you tire — never to failure.

good: Reach the opposite arm and leg long, not high
Back stays flat, as if a glass of water sat on it
bad: Lifting the leg above hip height and arching

exercises.name: Supine Rest, Calves Elevated
exercises.note: No rolling and no back stretch here on purpose — a sore back wants unloading, not pressure.

good: Calves on a chair, knees at ninety, arms out wide
Let the lower back go completely heavy
bad: Pulling your knees to your chest instead

good: In through the nose for four, out for eight
Only the hand on your belly should move
